The one who says this to you is he who serves you and shares your labors; and so he is “your hand.”
The one who says this to you is perhaps he who supports you, who lifts you up from a low earthly state; and so he is “your foot.”
Cast them all aside, cut them off, throw them all away from you; do not consent to them.
Answer such men as he answered who was advised to give false witness.

So you answer too; say to the man who says to you, “See, it is in Christian times that there are such pressing troubles, that the whole world is laid waste”; answer him, “And Christ foretold this to me before it came to pass.”
8. For why are you disturbed?
Your heart is disturbed by the pressing troubles of the world, as that ship was in which Christ was asleep.
Look, what is the reason, stout-hearted man, that your heart is disturbed?
That ship in which Christ is asleep is the heart in which faith is asleep.
For what new thing, what new thing, I ask, is told you, Christian?
“In Christian times the world is laid waste, the world is failing.”
Did not your Lord tell you the world shall be laid waste?
Did not your Lord tell you the world shall fail?
Why, when the promise was made, did you believe, and are disturbed now, when it is being fulfilled?
So then, the storm beats furiously against your heart; beware of shipwreck; wake up Christ.
The Apostle says, “that Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith.”
Christ dwells in you by faith.
Present faith is Christ present; waking faith is Christ awake; slumbering faith is Christ asleep.
Arise and stir yourself; say, “Lord, we perish.”
See what the Heathen say to us; and, what is worse, what evil Christians say!
Awake, O Lord, we perish.
Let your faith awake, and Christ begins to speak to you: “‘Why are you troubled?’
I told you beforehand of all these things.
I foretold them, so that when evils came, you might hope for good things, so that you might not faint in the evil.”
Do you wonder that the world is failing?
Wonder that the world has grown old.
It is like a man who is born, and grows up, and grows old.
There are many complaints in old age: the cough, the phlegm, the weakness of the eyes, fretfulness, and weariness.
So then, as when a man is old he is full of complaints, so the world is old and is full of troubles.
Is it a little thing that God has done for you, in that in the world’s old age He has sent Christ to you, that He may renew you then, when all is failing?
Do you not know that He signified this in the seed of Abraham?
“The seed of Abraham,” says the Apostle, “which is Christ.
He does not say, And to seeds, as of many; but as of One, And to your seed, which is Christ.”
Therefore a son was born to Abraham in his old age, because Christ was to come in the old age of this world.
He came when all things were growing old, and made them new.
As a made, created, perishing thing, the world was now declining to its fall.
It could not but abound in troubles; He came both to console you in the midst of present troubles and to promise you everlasting rest.

Do not choose, then, to cling to this aged world and to be unwilling to grow young in Christ, who tells you, “The world is perishing, the world is growing old, the world is failing; it is distressed by the heavy breathing of old age.
But do not fear: ‘Your youth shall be renewed like the eagle’s.’”
9. See, they say, it is in Christian times that Rome perishes.
Perhaps Rome is not perishing; perhaps she is only scourged, not utterly destroyed; perhaps she is chastened, not brought to nothing.
It may be so; Rome will not perish if the Romans do not perish.
And perish they will not if they praise God; perish they will if they blaspheme Him.
For what is Rome, but the Romans?
For the question is not of her wood and stones, of her lofty free-standing palaces, and all her spacious walls.
All this was made only on this condition: that it should fall some day.
When man built it, he laid stone on stone; and when man destroyed it, he removed stone from stone.
Man made it; man destroyed it.
Is any injury done to Rome because it is said, “She is falling”?
No, not to Rome, but to her builder perhaps.
Do we, then, do its builder any injury because we say that Rome is falling, which Romulus built?
This world itself, which God built, will be burned with fire.
But neither does what man has made fall to ruin except when God wills it, nor what God has made, except when He wills.
For if the work of man does not fall without God’s will, how can God’s work fall by the will of man?
Yet God made the world that was one day to fall for you; and therefore He made you as one who was one day to die.

Man himself, the city’s ornament, man himself, the city’s inhabitant, ruler, governor, comes on this condition, that he may go; is born on this condition, that he may die; entered the world on this condition, that he may pass away; “Heaven and earth shall pass away”: what wonder, then, if some time or other there should be an end of a single city?
And yet perhaps the city’s end has not come now; yet some time or other come it will.
But why does Rome perish amid the sacrifices of Christians?
Why was her mother Troy burned amid the sacrifices of Heathens?
The gods in whom the Romans have placed all their hope, yes, the Roman gods in whom the Heathen Romans placed their hope, moved from the flames of Troy to found Rome.
These very gods of Rome were originally the gods of Troy.
Troy was burned, and Aeneas took the fugitive gods; or rather, himself a fugitive, he carried away these senseless gods.
For they could be carried by the fugitive; but they could not flee away themselves.
And coming with these gods into Italy, with these false gods, he founded Rome.
It is too long to go through the whole story; yet I would briefly mention what their own writings contain.

An author of theirs well known to all speaks thus: “As I have received the account, the Trojans, who under the leadership of Aeneas were wandering about as fugitives without any settled home, originally built and inhabited Rome.”
So they had their gods with them; they built Rome in Latium, and there they placed the gods to be worshiped which had before been worshiped in Troy.
Juno is brought in by their poet, incensed against Aeneas and the fugitive Trojans, saying,

blocks.x:
“A race of wandering slaves, abhorred by me,
With prosperous passage cuts the Tuscan sea;
To fruitful Italy their course they steer,
And for their vanquished gods design new temples there.”

s: Now when these vanquished gods were carried into Italy, was it as a protecting deity, or as an omen of their future fall?
“Love,” therefore, “the law of God, and nothing shall be an offense to you.”

We pray you, we beg you, we exhort you: be meek, sympathize with the suffering, bear with the weak; and on this occasion of the gathering of so many strangers, and needy, and suffering people, let your hospitality and your good works abound.
Only let Christians do what Christ commands, and then the Heathen will blaspheme only to their own hurt.
